sentence: If only the apartment had a balcony!
setupText: The apartment has no balcony. What does the speaker express?
taskText: If only the apartment had a balcony!
text: The apartment has no balcony. What does the speaker express? If only the apartment had a balcony!
options: A condition that the apartment already satisfies.
A strong wish for something the apartment lacks.
A claim about a balcony removed last year.
An instruction to inspect an existing balcony.
answer: A strong wish for something the apartment lacks.
focusKey: coverage-subjunctive-and-unreal-forms-b1-3643:If only as an emphatic unfulfilled present wish
explanation: If only adds emphasis to the wish for a different present situation.

rationales.A condition that the apartment already s: The context says there is no balcony; if only does not assert that the condition is satisfied.
rationales.A claim about a balcony removed last yea: Had in this wish concerns the desired present state, not a stated removal in the past.
rationales.An instruction to inspect an existing ba: The sentence wishes for a balcony rather than instructing anyone to inspect one.
rationales.A strong wish for something the apartmen: If only adds emphasis to the wish for a different present situation.

rationales.could to hear: To is not used between could and hear.

sentence: Choose a conditional plan, not an unconditional arrangement or a report of a finished repair.
setupText: The roof has not yet been repaired. Which sentence makes using the attic depend on a possible repair?
taskText: Choose a conditional plan, not an unconditional arrangement or a report of a finished repair.
text: The roof has not yet been repaired. Which sentence makes using the attic depend on a possible repair? Choose a conditional plan, not an unconditional arrangement or a report of a finished repair.
options: We will use the attic whether or not the roof is repaired.
We are using the attic because the roof has been repaired.
We will use the attic if the roof is repaired.
We used the attic after the roof was repaired.
answer: We will use the attic if the roof is repaired.
focusKey: coverage-subjunctive-and-unreal-forms-b1-3649:Open future condition distinguished from unconditional and completed-event accounts
explanation: If makes using the attic depend on the possible repair without asserting that it has occurred.

rationales.We will use the attic whether or not the: Whether or not removes repair as a condition for using the attic.
rationales.We will use the attic if the roof is rep: If makes using the attic depend on the possible repair without asserting that it has occurred.
rationales.We are using the attic because the roof: Because treats the repair as completed and gives a current use, contrary to the context.
rationales.We used the attic after the roof was rep: This reports a finished sequence rather than a possible future plan.

explanation: Had booked imagines an earlier booking in a past that can no longer be changed.

rationales.book: Book is not the past-perfect form used for this regret about an earlier decision.
rationales.would book: Would book looks to a desired future behavior rather than undoing the completed late booking.
rationales.had booked: Had booked imagines an earlier booking in a past that can no longer be changed.
rationales.am booking: Am booking describes a current activity rather than regret about the earlier event.

rationales.would hear: Would hear does not form the past-perfect condition requested here.
rationales.have heard: Have heard is present perfect, not the past perfect locating the unreal hearing before the missed arrival.
rationales.had heard: Had heard gives the unreal past condition that would have changed the arrival outcome.

sentence: He talks as if he owned the place.
setupText: The guest is visiting the gallery for the first time. What does this description suggest?
taskText: He talks as if he owned the place.
text: The guest is visiting the gallery for the first time. What does this description suggest? He talks as if he owned the place.
options: His manner resembles that of an owner, although the context does not make him one.
He owned the gallery before becoming a guest.
He has just bought the gallery.
He is giving instructions for selling the gallery.
answer: His manner resembles that of an owner, although the context does not make him one.
focusKey: coverage-subjunctive-and-unreal-forms-b1-3654:As-if comparison distinguished from factual past ownership
explanation: As if compares his way of speaking with an imagined owner's manner rather than asserting ownership.

rationales.He owned the gallery before becoming a g: Owned after as if can describe an unreal present comparison; it does not establish former ownership.
The description of his manner does not report a purchase.
rationales.His manner resembles that of an owner, a: As if compares his way of speaking with an imagined owner's manner rather than asserting ownership.
rationales.He is giving instructions for selling th: The sentence describes how he talks, not the specific content of a sale instruction.

sentence: A: 'I wish I was taller.' B: 'I wish I were taller.' Which comparison is accurate?
setupText: Consider these versions in ordinary informal English.
taskText: A: 'I wish I was taller.' B: 'I wish I were taller.' Which comparison is accurate?
text: Consider these versions in ordinary informal English. A: 'I wish I was taller.' B: 'I wish I were taller.' Which comparison is accurate?
options: A refers to a past wish; B expresses a present wish.
A expresses a present wish; B expresses a past wish.
Both can express the same present wish.
Only B can express this wish in informal English.
answer: Both can express the same present wish.
focusKey: coverage-subjunctive-and-unreal-forms-b1-3655:Informal was and irrealis were recognized in singular present wishes
explanation: Both express a wish about present height. Were is the conventional irrealis form and also suits formal styles.

rationales.A refers to a past wish; B expresses a p: Was can express the present unreal wish here; it need not place the wish in the past.
rationales.A expresses a present wish; B expresses: Were also expresses a wish about current height here, not a past wish.
rationales.Only B can express this wish in informal: Was is a standard informal alternative in this singular wish clause, so A should not be excluded.
Both express a wish about present height. Were is the conventional irrealis form and also suits formal styles.
